facts.statement: Cryodrakon boreas was named and described in 2019 by paleontologists David Hone, Michael Habib, and François Therrien.
facts.quote: But it was not until 2019 that it received a new genus and type species, Cryodrakon boreas, named and described by paleontologists David Hone, Michael Habib, and François Therrien.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon lived in what is now Canada during the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 76.7 to 74.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Cryodrakon is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the late Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Canada, around 76.7 and 74.3 million years ago.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of Cryodrakon was uncovered in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta in 1992.
facts.quote: In 1992, a partial pterosaur skeleton was uncovered in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta.

facts.statement: Bones of large azhdarchid pterosaurs have been reported from Alberta since 1972.
facts.quote: Since 1972, bones of large pterosaurs (flying reptiles) belonging to the family Azhdarchidae have been reported from Alberta.

facts.statement: Early fossils of Cryodrakon from Alberta were often assigned to the genus Quetzalcoatlus due to limited information about North American azhdarchids at the time.
facts.quote: They were sometimes referred to as Quetzalcoatlus sp., indicating an uncertain species of Quetzalcoatlus, or were just assigned to Quetzalcoatlus without specifying anything.

facts.statement: Fossil bones of Cryodrakon show tooth marks and an embedded tooth tip, likely from the predator Saurornitholestes langstoni.
facts.quote: They noticed that the bones had tooth marks and even a broken tip of a tooth imbedded in one of them, most likely coming from Saurornitholestes langstoni of the same formation.

facts.statement: The Cryodrakon skeleton found in Canada is the only pterosaur fossil in the country consisting of more than a single bone.
facts.quote: This is the only pterosaur found in Canada with fossil remains that consist of more than just a single bone so far.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen TMP 1992.83 lacks a skull but includes a neck vertebra, rib, humerus, pteroid bone, metacarpal, tibia, and metatarsal.
facts.quote: This partial skeleton, specimen TMP 1992.83, lacks the skull and consists of a fourth cervical (neck) vertebra, a rib, a humerus, a pteroid bone, a fourth metacarpal, a tibia and a metatarsal.

facts.statement: Specimen TMP 1992.83 became the holotype for the new species Cryodrakon boreas in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, specimen TMP 1992.83 received a new separate genus and type species, Cryodrakon boreas, and became the holotype of this new pterosaur.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that all azhdarchid remains from Alberta belong to a single distinct taxon, Cryodrakon boreas.
facts.quote: Through comparisons with other azhdarchid taxa, Hone and colleagues concluded that all azhdarchid material from Alberta could be referred to a single distinct taxon.

facts.statement: The name Cryodrakon means "cold dragon" in Greek, referencing Canada, while boreas refers to the Greek god of the north winds.
facts.quote: Its generic name means "cold dragon" in Ancient Greek, in reference to its Canadian origin, while its specific name refers to the Greek god of the north winds, Boreas.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon boreas translates to "cold dragon of the north winds".
facts.quote: Hence, Cryodrakon boreas could be translated as "cold dragon of the north winds".

facts.statement: Most known Cryodrakon fossils are from young or subadult individuals, suggesting a wingspan of about 5 meters.
facts.quote: Most of the fossil remains of Cryodrakon belong to either young or subadult individuals, from which a wingspan of about 5 m could be estimated.

facts.statement: A large incomplete neck vertebra measuring 40 cm suggests that adult Cryodrakon could have had a vertebra at least 50 cm long.
facts.quote: However, much larger fossils have been unearthed, including an incomplete fifth cervical (neck) vertebra that measures 40 cm. If complete, it could have measured at least 50 cm.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon is estimated to have had a wingspan of about 10 meters, making it one of the largest flying animals in history.
facts.quote: A wingspan of about 10 m is the most commonly estimated for Cryodrakon, which makes it one of the largest flying animals to ever exist.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon is classified within the pterosaur family Azhdarchidae, which includes Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: In its description, Cryodrakon was assigned to family Azhdarchidae, which includes the already mentioned Quetzalcoatlus.

facts.statement: Later studies placed Cryodrakon within the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae, though its exact position varies between analyses.
facts.quote: Subsequent phylogenetic analyses would place it within the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae, though in varying position depending on the study.

facts.statement: Researchers noted features that exclude Cryodrakon from a basal position within Azhdarchidae, though a full phylogenetic analysis was not performed due to fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis was not performed due to the fragmentary nature of its remains, but the describers pointed out certain features that would exclude Cryodrakon from being in a basal (primitive) position within Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon had a minimum estimated wingspan of 5 meters based on its smaller fossil remains.
facts.quote: A wingspan of at least 5 m has been set for Cryodrakon based on these smaller remains.

facts.statement: A juvenile Cryodrakon specimen with a 10.6 mm fifth cervical vertebra was estimated to have a wingspan of about 2 meters.
facts.quote: specimen TMP 1996.12.369, a fifth cervical vertebra with a length of only 10.6 mm, is from a juvenile Cryodrakon, which was given an estimated wingspan of about 2 m.

facts.statement: Adult Cryodrakon are estimated to have had a wingspan of about 10 meters.
facts.quote: A wingspan of about 10 m has been estimated for adult individuals.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon is distinguished from other azhdarchids by two specific features of its neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: Cryodrakon is distinguished from all other known azhdarchids by two features of its neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon's postexapophyses were wide and short, separated from the cotyle, with facets directed downwards.
facts.quote: The postexapophyses of Cryodrakon were prominent in width but short in length, clearly separated from the cotyle, and their facets were directed downwards.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon had a body structure similar to Quetzalcoatlus but with more robust bones, suggesting it was slightly heavier.
facts.quote: In terms of body structure, Cryodrakon was proportionally similar to Quetzalcoatlus and other long-necked advanced members of the Azhdarchidae, though its somewhat more robust bones may indicate that it was slightly heavier.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon is classified within the family Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: In its description, Hone and colleagues placed Cryodrakon in the family Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: The genus Cryodrakon was described by Hone and colleagues in 2019.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Hone et al., 2019

facts.statement: The only known species of Cryodrakon is Cryodrakon boreas.
facts.quote: species: Cryodrakon boreas

facts.statement: Cryodrakon lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Cryodrakon, meaning "cold dragon of the north wind," was an extinct azhdarchid pterosaur that lived in what is now Canada during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Cryodrakon (que significa "dragón frío del viento del norte") es un género extinto de pterosaurio azdárquido que vivió durante el período Cretácico Superior en lo que ahora es Canadá.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cryodrakon boreas have been found in the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: Solo se conoce a una especie, C. boreas, cuyos restos fueron hallados en la Formación Dinosaur Park.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon likely hunted smaller animals on the ground, similar to modern marabou storks.
facts.quote: Azhdarchid pterosaurs similar to Cryodrakon are currently thought to have fed by hunting for smaller animals while on the ground, similar to modern day marabou storks.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Cryodrakon showed evidence of being scavenged by a dromaeosaurid, possibly Saurornitholestes langstoni.
facts.quote: The holotype partial skeleton of Cryodrakon was found to have been scavenged by a dromaeosaurid, possibly Saurornitholestes langstoni.

facts.statement: A broken tooth found in a Cryodrakon bone suggests its thin-walled bones were very tough.
facts.quote: Aside from tooth marks, a broken tooth was found in one of the bones, which, according to the authors, meant that the thin-walled bone of Cryodrakon "must have been very tough."

facts.statement: A 2025 study found probable bite marks on a juvenile Cryodrakon vertebra from various possible predators or scavengers.
facts.quote: In 2025, a fifth cervical vertebra of a juvenile Cryodrakon (TMP 2023.012.0237) showed probable bite marks from either Champsosaurus, Leidyosuchus, Albertochampsa, a Stangerochampsa-like taxon, or possibly Eodelphis.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon fossils come from the Dinosaur Park Formation, which preserves alluvial and coastal plain environments.
facts.quote: The Dinosaur Park Formation, where fossils of Cryodrakon have been excavated, preserves many fossils from alluvial and coastal plain environments.

facts.statement: The environment where Cryodrakon lived experienced high precipitation, warm temperatures, and humidity, becoming increasingly swamp-like over time.
facts.quote: Both of these environments would have experienced high precipitation, warm temperatures, and high humidity, with conditions becoming more swamp-like as time progressed.

facts.statement: The precise phylogenetic relationship of Cryodrakon with other azhdarchids remains unclear as no exact cladistic analysis was initially provided.
facts.quote: No exact cladistic analysis had been given to clarify its precise relationship with other azhdarchids.

facts.statement: The species Cryodrakon boreas was named and described in 2019 by David William Elliott Hone, Michael Habib, and François Therrien.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon's lateral pneumatic foramina were positioned near the lower edge of the neural canal, whereas in other azhdarchids they were located much higher.

facts.statement: Cryodrakon's postexapophyses were wide but short, clearly separated from the cotylus, and their facets faced downward.
facts.quote: Las postexapófisis de Cryodrakon eran prominentes en cuanto a su ancho pero su longitud era corta, estaban claramente separadas del cotilo, y sus facetas se dirigían hacia abajo.
